course_description:
Elective project for students enrolled in Master of Educational Studies. Project topics are confined to specialised research and teaching interests of permanent staff of the School of Education. Students must choose and approach a potential supervisor. Projects are negotiated with supervisors and typically take the form of literature reviews or small research projects. Students and supervisors together complete the Application to Undertake a Supervised Research Project Form located on the School website (Educational Studies - Postgraduate Coursework). Forms should be submitted two weeks prior to the enrolment due date for the chosen semester to the Administrative Officer. Subsequent for approval to undertake the project being received from the School of Education, students enrol in the course. Students completing a project in one semester enrol in EDUC7910. Students completing a project over one year commencing in semester 1 enrol in EDUC7700 in both semesters. Students completing a project over one year commencing in semester 2 enrol in EDUC7710 in both semesters. Students are expected to maintain contact with their supervisor.

To request permission to enrol, submit research project application form to education@uq.edu.au two weeks prior to enrolment due date.

Projects provide an opportunity for students to undertake an independent study on a topic of their interest under the supervision of an academic from the School of Education. Students who wish to complete a project must negotiate their topic and project requirements directly with their supervisor. An Application to Undertake a Supervised Research Project form, which includes a synopsis of the proposed project, must be completed and submitted two weeks prior to the enrolment due date for the chosen semester.

The project will be assessed by your supervisor and one additional marker.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of concepts and issues in educational research
Demonstrate analysis and synthesis of concepts and issues in educational research
Provide written explanations and analyses that are clear, logical, convincing, concise and free of textual errors
Demonstrate specialised knowledge in a field of educational research

assessment_details.title: Task 1 Project Plan
assessment_details.task_description: Task 1: Individual Project Plan (Abstract, annotated bibliography, timeline) (Total words for Task 1 = 1000 words) a) Write an abstract that provides a rationale for your project. (100-150 words) b) Prepare an annotated bibliography containing at least 8 references that you will use during your project (approximately 100 words per reference in which you provide a short summary and critique of the topic in the reference) c) Prepare a project timeline that outlines the tasks you will complete to ensure the timely submission of your project. These tasks will be negotiated with your supervisor. If you use AI and/or machine translation (MT) tools in preparing your presentation resources such as ppt slides, script and notes, you must provide clear and specific details about how they were used. Failure to acknowledge the use of generative AI or MT may constitute academic misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. assessment_details.title: Task 2 Project Report
assessment_details.task_description: This task is the write up of the completed project. Students are expected to keep in contact with their supervisor to ensure that this task is of enough depth and scope to meet the requirements expected of a review of the literature or a report on a study that the student has implemented. Submit your completed project, including title page, table of contents, written project, reference list and any appendices. (10,000 words) NB: The Criteria Sheet used for marking your project will depend on the nature of your project. If your project is literature based, then the Literature Review Criteria Sheet will be used. If you conduct a research project, then the Criteria Sheet for Research Projects will be used. assessment_details.title: Task 3: Oral Defence
assessment_details.task_description: Following project report submission, you will participate in an Oral Defence of your research project. The format involves: A three-minute overview of the thesis by the candidate 10 - 12 minutes Question and Answer (no preparation). The Oral Defence will be conducted by the Thesis Supervisor and the second examiner. They will negotiate an appropriate time after submission of project report. You will be provided with a slide deck to assist you to prepare your three-minute thesis overview. The Oral Defence will be recorded and assessed on a pass/fail basis against the following criteria: Demonstrated ability to articulate the central research question/s, key gap in knowledge the thesis addresses, and central hypothesis. Demonstrated ability to justify the thesis structure. Demonstrated ability to explain and justify the methodology/ies used. Demonstrated mastery of knowledge, analysis and findings presented in the thesis. Ability to satisfactorily respond to spontaneous and pertinent questions in the oral defence. learning_activities.topic: Research Project Projects provide an opportunity to undertake independent study under the supervision of an academic from the School of Education. You are expected to maintain regular contact with your supervisor for input and feedback. In EDUC7910, your learning is shaped in partnership with your supervisor rather than prescribed. As projects vary widely, you are responsible for actively directing your learning. You are expected to: Discuss and clarify your project goals and expectations with your supervisor. Co-develop a plan aligned with course learning and assessments. Define your project scope, including research questions, methods, timelines, and outputs. Seek and respond to feedback regularly. Take responsibility for your progress and engagement. Supervision is a collaborative process. You are expected to engage as an active participant and approach supervision as a professional dialogue marked by preparation, initiative, and reflection. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
